question: Who was the founder of a non-violent movement named as “Khudai Khidmatgars”?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Khudai Khidmatgar (“Servants of God”) movement was founded in 1929 by Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan among the Pathans of the North-West Frontier Province (NWFP). (खुदाई खिदमतगार — ईश्वर के सेवक)

• Its members were called Red Shirts (Surkh Posh) because of their brick-red uniforms, and they were pledged to non-violence (ahimsa).

• Ghaffar Khan is popularly known as Frontier Gandhi / Badshah Khan / Sarhadi Gandhi; he was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 1987, the first non-Indian to receive it.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• C. Rajagopalachari — last Governor-General of India and the first Indian to hold that post; founder of the Swatantra Party (1959).

• Mohammad Ali Jinnah — leader of the Muslim League, founder of Pakistan, known as Quaid-e-Azam.

• Mahatma Gandhi — led the Champaran (1917), Non-Cooperation (1920), Civil Disobedience (1930) and Quit India (1942) movements.

NOTE

• Ghaffar Khan’s Khudai Khidmatgars gave the Congress its strongest base in the NWFP during the Civil Disobedience Movement, notably the Qissa Khwani Bazaar massacre, Peshawar (1930).

• Ghaffar Khan’s autobiography is ‘My Life and Struggle’.

question: Which of the following metal is always a component in an amalgam?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mercury.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• An amalgam is an alloy of mercury (Hg) with one or more other metals; therefore mercury is always present in an amalgam. (अमलगम — पारद मिश्रधातु)

• Mercury is the only metal that is liquid at room temperature; its symbol Hg comes from *hydrargyrum*. It readily dissolves gold, silver, zinc and tin to form amalgams.

• Dental amalgam (silver–tin–copper + mercury) is used for filling teeth; sodium amalgam is used as a reducing agent in organic chemistry.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Iron, platinum, tungsten and tantalum do not form amalgams with mercury — that is why mercury is stored and transported in iron containers.

• Zinc forms an amalgam used in the Clemmensen reduction, but zinc itself is not a compulsory component of every amalgam.

• Aluminium and Strontium are highly reactive metals and are not the defining component of an amalgam.

NOTE

• Common alloys for exams: Brass = Cu + Zn; Bronze = Cu + Sn; Stainless steel = Fe + Cr + Ni; Solder = Pb + Sn; German silver = Cu + Zn + Ni.

question: Bhimbetka caves are situated in which of the following states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Madhya Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Bhimbetka rock shelters are located in the Raisen district of Madhya Pradesh, in the foothills of the Vindhya range. (भीमबेटका — शैलाश्रय)

• They contain prehistoric (Palaeolithic and Mesolithic) rock paintings, the earliest traces of human life on the Indian subcontinent, and were discovered by Dr. V. S. Wakankar in 1957.

• Bhimbetka was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2003.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Other UNESCO sites in Madhya Pradesh — Khajuraho temples (1986) and Buddhist Monuments at Sanchi (1989).

• Rajasthan — Hill Forts of Rajasthan, Jantar Mantar (Jaipur), Keoladeo National Park, Jaipur City.

• Gujarat — Champaner-Pavagadh, Rani-ki-Vav (Patan), Historic City of Ahmedabad, Dholavira.

NOTE

• Famous caves and their states: Ajanta & Ellora – Maharashtra, Elephanta – Maharashtra, Udayagiri-Khandagiri – Odisha, Barabar (oldest rock-cut) – Bihar, Borra – Andhra Pradesh.

question: Treasury bills are issued by the ________.
option_1: Securities and Exchange Board of India
solution_text:
The correct answer is Government of India.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Treasury Bills (T-bills) are short-term debt instruments of the Government of India; the RBI merely issues them on behalf of the Central Government as its banker and debt manager. (राजकोषीय बिल)

• They are issued at a discount and redeemed at face value; the difference is the investor’s return, so T-bills are zero-coupon securities (no interest is paid separately).

• T-bills are currently issued in three tenors — 91-day, 182-day and 364-day — with a minimum amount of ₹10,000.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• RBI — the central bank (est. 1 April 1935); it conducts the auctions of T-bills but the borrower/issuer is the Government.

• SEBI — regulator of the securities market, established 1988, statutory in 1992.

• IRDAI — regulator of insurance, established in 1999, headquartered at Hyderabad.

NOTE

• Other money-market instruments: Commercial Paper (issued by companies), Certificate of Deposit (issued by banks), Call money, Cash Management Bills (CMBs).

• T-bills are considered risk-free because they carry a sovereign guarantee.

question: National Tribal Dance Festival 2022 was held in which place?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Raipur.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The National Tribal Dance Festival 2022 (3rd edition) was organised at Raipur, the capital of Chhattisgarh, in November 2022. (राष्ट्रीय जनजातीय नृत्य महोत्सव)

• The festival is held around Chhattisgarh Rajyotsava (1 November), the state’s foundation day, and features tribal dance troupes from Indian states as well as foreign countries.

• Chhattisgarh was carved out of Madhya Pradesh on 1 November 2000; it has a very large Scheduled Tribe population.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Jaipur (Rajasthan) — known for the Jaipur Literature Festival and the Teej and Elephant festivals.

• Puri (Odisha) — famous for the Jagannath Rath Yatra and the Puri Beach Festival.

• Pune (Maharashtra) — associated with the Sawai Gandharva Bhimsen Mahotsav (classical music).

NOTE

• Chhattisgarh static GK: Capital — Raipur; Chief Minister (2022) — Bhupesh Baghel; famous dance forms — Panthi, Raut Nacha, Karma, Saila; Chitrakote Falls is called the ‘Niagara of India’.

question: According to the Competition Amendment Bill, 2022, the penalty for gun-jumping is proposed to be ______ of the deal value.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1%.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Competition (Amendment) Bill, 2022 proposed raising the penalty for gun-jumping to 1% of the total turnover or the deal value, whichever is applicable. (गन-जम्पिंग — स्वीकृति से पहले सौदा पूरा करना)

• Gun-jumping means consummating (giving effect to) a combination — merger or acquisition — before receiving the approval of the Competition Commission of India (CCI).

• The Bill also introduced a deal value threshold: transactions above ₹2,000 crore with substantial business operations in India must be notified to the CCI.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Bill amends the Competition Act, 2002, and reduced the time limit for CCI approval of combinations from 210 days to 150 days.

• The Competition Commission of India (CCI) was established in 2003 and became fully functional in 2009; its headquarters is in New Delhi.

• The Bill was introduced in the Lok Sabha in August 2022 and was enacted as the Competition (Amendment) Act, 2023.

NOTE

• CCI works to prevent anti-competitive agreements, abuse of dominant position and regulate combinations; appeals against CCI orders lie with the NCLAT.

question: The Chief Minister of which of the following states launched the second phase of Ladli Laxmi Scheme 2.0 in November 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Madhya Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Ladli Laxmi Yojana 2.0 is a scheme of the Madhya Pradesh government, launched by then Chief Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan. (लाडली लक्ष्मी योजना)

• The original Ladli Laxmi Yojana was launched in 2007 to improve the sex ratio, check female foeticide and support the education and marriage of girl children.

• Phase 2.0 extends the benefit beyond Class 12 — assisting girls with college/higher-education fees and providing financial help at graduation.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Uttar Pradesh — runs the Kanya Sumangala Yojana for girl children.

• Bihar — runs the Mukhyamantri Kanya Utthan Yojana and the Mukhyamantri Cycle Yojana.

• Andhra Pradesh — runs Amma Vodi and YSR Cheyutha for women and mothers.

NOTE

• Central girl-child schemes: Beti Bachao Beti Padhao (2015, from Panipat, Haryana), Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana (2015), CBSE Udaan and Balika Samriddhi Yojana.

question: ‘Golden Girl’ is the autobiography of ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is P.T. Usha.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• ‘Golden Girl’ is the autobiography of the legendary Indian athlete P. T. Usha (Pilavullakandi Thekkeparambil Usha) of Kerala. (स्वर्ण बालिका)

• She is nicknamed the ‘Payyoli Express’ and the ‘Queen of Indian Track and Field’; at the 1984 Los Angeles Olympics she missed a bronze in the 400 m hurdles by 1/100th of a second.

• She was awarded the Arjuna Award (1984) and the Padma Shri (1985), and became President of the Indian Olympic Association (IOA) in December 2022 — its first woman President.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Divya Dutta — actress; wrote ‘Me and Ma’.

• Saina Nehwal — badminton star; her biography is ‘Playing to Win’.

• Neena Gupta — actress; her autobiography is ‘Sach Kahun Toh’.

NOTE

• Sports autobiographies for exams: ‘Playing It My Way’ – Sachin Tendulkar, ‘The Race of My Life’ – Milkha Singh, ‘Unbreakable’ – Mary Kom, ‘Ace Against Odds’ – Sania Mirza, ‘Straight from the Heart’ – Kapil Dev.

question: In the Indian subcontinent, how many country/countries share its land frontiers with every member country of the subcontinent?
solution_text:
The correct answer is One.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Only one country — India — shares its land frontiers with every neighbouring member country of the Indian subcontinent. (भारतीय उपमहाद्वीप)

• India shares land borders with Pakistan, Afghanistan, China, Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh and Myanmar — 7 countries in all; Sri Lanka and Maldives are island nations separated by sea.

• No other subcontinental country touches all the others; for example, Nepal and Bhutan are landlocked between only India and China.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• India’s longest land border is with Bangladesh (≈ 4,096 km), followed by China (≈ 3,488 km) and Pakistan (≈ 3,323 km); the shortest is with Afghanistan (≈ 106 km).

• The border with Pakistan is called the Radcliffe Line (1947), with China the McMahon Line (1914), and with Bangladesh also the Radcliffe Line.

• India is separated from Sri Lanka by the Palk Strait and Gulf of Mannar.

NOTE

• State touching the most countries: Sikkim and West Bengal border three countries each; Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal, Sikkim, Uttarakhand touch Nepal.

question: How many Fundamental Duties were added in the Constitution of India by the 42nd Amendment?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 10.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976 added 10 Fundamental Duties in Part IVA, Article 51A of the Constitution. (मूल कर्तव्य)

• They were incorporated on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee (1976) and were inspired by the Constitution of the erstwhile USSR.

• The 86th Amendment Act, 2002 added the 11th duty — the duty of a parent/guardian to provide educational opportunities to a child between 6 and 14 years — making the present total 11.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The 42nd Amendment is called the ‘Mini-Constitution’; it added the words Socialist, Secular and Integrity to the Preamble.

• Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable — they cannot be enforced by courts.

• The 86th Amendment, 2002 also inserted Article 21A (Right to Education).

NOTE

• Related borrowings: Fundamental Rights – USA, Directive Principles – Ireland, Fundamental Duties – erstwhile USSR, Parliamentary system – Britain, Emergency provisions – Germany (Weimar).

question: Which among the following books was written by Dr. Raghuram Rajan?
solution_text:
The correct answer is The Third Pillar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• ‘The Third Pillar: How Markets and the State Leave the Community Behind’ (2019) was written by Dr. Raghuram Rajan, economist and former Governor of the Reserve Bank of India (2013–2016).

• The book argues that the community is the neglected ‘third pillar’ alongside the state and the markets.

• Rajan’s other well-known works include ‘Fault Lines’ (2010), ‘Saving Capitalism from the Capitalists’ (with Luigi Zingales) and ‘I Do What I Do’ (2017).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• ‘We Are Displaced’ — by Malala Yousafzai, Nobel Peace Prize winner (2014).

• ‘The India Story’ — by Bimal Jalan, former RBI Governor.

• ‘My Life in Full: Work, Family and Our Future’ — by Indra Nooyi, former CEO of PepsiCo.

NOTE

• Rajan famously predicted the 2008 global financial crisis at the Jackson Hole conference in 2005, and served as Chief Economist of the IMF.

• He introduced the Asset Quality Review (AQR) of Indian banks as RBI Governor.

question: Dilwara Temple is one of the finest and architecturally renowned ______ temples in India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jain.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Dilwara Temples are a group of five Jain temples at Mount Abu, Sirohi district, Rajasthan, built between the 11th and 13th centuries CE in white marble. (दिलवाड़ा मंदिर — जैन मंदिर)

• The Vimal Vasahi temple (dedicated to Adinath, the 1st Tirthankara) was built in 1031 CE by Vimal Shah, a minister of the Solanki ruler Bhima I.

• The Luna Vasahi temple (dedicated to Neminath, the 22nd Tirthankara) was built in 1230 CE by the brothers Vastupala and Tejpal. The temples are famous for their intricate marble carving.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Other famous Jain sites: Shravanabelagola (Gommateshwara/Bahubali statue), Karnataka, Ranakpur temple, Rajasthan, Palitana temples, Gujarat, Khandagiri–Udayagiri, Odisha.

• Mount Abu is the only hill station of Rajasthan, located in the Aravalli range; Guru Shikhar is its highest peak.

NOTE

• Jainism: founded/reformed by Mahavira, the 24th Tirthankara; the 1st was Rishabhanatha (Adinath) and the 23rd was Parshvanatha. Its three jewels (Triratna) are Right Faith, Right Knowledge and Right Conduct.

question: Which Indian music composer received his second Grammy award in 2022 for the album ‘Divine Tides’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ricky Kej.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Ricky Kej, the Bengaluru-based composer and environmentalist, won his second Grammy Award in 2022 for the album ‘Divine Tides’, made with the legendary drummer Stewart Copeland of *The Police*.

• The award was in the Best New Age Album category; his first Grammy (2015) was for the album ‘Winds of Samsara’ with Wouter Kellerman.

• He won a third Grammy in 2023 for the ‘Divine Tides’ live/immersive version, in the Best Immersive Audio Album category.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• P. A. Deepak — sound engineer who won a Grammy (2010) for *Slumdog Millionaire*’s ‘Jai Ho’.

• Tanvi Shah — the first Indian woman to win a Grammy (2010), also for ‘Jai Ho’, for which she wrote and sang the Spanish lyrics.

• Manoj George — violinist who shared the 2015 Grammy for *Winds of Samsara*.

NOTE

• Indian Grammy winners: Pandit Ravi Shankar (first Indian, 1968), Zakir Hussain, A. R. Rahman (2 Grammys, 2010), Vishwa Mohan Bhatt, Ricky Kej, and Shankar Mahadevan/Shakti (2024).

question: Which freedom fighter was involved in the Kakori Train Action in 1925, for which the British government condemned him to death?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ram Prasad Bismil.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Kakori Train Action (Kakori Conspiracy) took place on 9 August 1925 near Kakori, Lucknow (Uttar Pradesh), when revolutionaries of the Hindustan Republican Association (HRA) looted a train carrying government treasury money. (काकोरी कांड)

• It was led by Ram Prasad Bismil, along with Ashfaqullah Khan, Rajendra Lahiri, Roshan Singh, Chandrashekhar Azad and others.

• Ram Prasad Bismil was hanged on 19 December 1927 at Gorakhpur jail; Ashfaqullah Khan (Faizabad) and Roshan Singh were hanged the same day, and Rajendra Lahiri on 17 December 1927. Chandrashekhar Azad escaped arrest.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Lala Hardayal — a founder of the Ghadar Party (1913, San Francisco).

• V. D. Savarkar — author of ‘The Indian War of Independence, 1857’; founder of Abhinav Bharat; imprisoned in the Cellular Jail, Andaman.

• Mahatma Gandhi followed non-violence and was never associated with revolutionary actions.

NOTE

• Bismil wrote the famous patriotic lines ‘Sarfaroshi ki tamanna ab hamare dil mein hai’ is attributed to Bismil Azimabadi but was popularised by Ram Prasad Bismil.

• The HRA was reorganised as the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA) in 1928 at Feroz Shah Kotla, Delhi.

question: As of 2022, which among the following countries is the largest importer of Indian iron ore?
solution_text:
The correct answer is China.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• China is by far the largest importer of Indian iron ore, accounting for the overwhelming share of India’s iron-ore exports; Japan and South Korea are the other significant buyers.

• China is also the world’s largest producer of crude steel, which drives its huge demand for iron ore. (लोह अयस्क)

• India’s iron ore is exported mainly through the ports of Paradip (Odisha), Visakhapatnam (Andhra Pradesh), Mormugao (Goa) and Mangaluru (Karnataka).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Leading iron-ore producing states in India: Odisha (largest), followed by Chhattisgarh, Karnataka and Jharkhand.

• Major iron-ore mines: Bailadila (Chhattisgarh), Kudremukh (Karnataka), Noamundi (Jharkhand), Barbil–Joda (Odisha).

• The best quality iron ore is magnetite (Fe3O4), while haematite (Fe2O3) is the most widely mined ore in India.

NOTE

• Australia and Brazil are the world’s largest exporters of iron ore; India is a comparatively small exporter but a large producer.

• The National Mineral Development Corporation (NMDC) is India’s largest iron-ore producer.

question: When was the first non-synchronous census conducted in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1872.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The first census in India was conducted in 1872 during the Viceroyalty of Lord Mayo; it was non-synchronous, i.e. it was not carried out simultaneously across the country. (गैर-एककालिक जनगणना)

• The first synchronous (simultaneous) census was held in 1881 under Lord Ripon, supervised by W. C. Plowden, and censuses have been held every 10 years since then.

• The Census of India is conducted by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner under the Ministry of Home Affairs, as per the Census Act, 1948.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The first census of independent India was held in 1951.

• Census 2011 was the 15th National Census and the 7th after independence; its motto was ‘Our Census, Our Future’.

• As per Census 2011: population 121.08 crore, sex ratio 943, literacy 74.04%, density 382 persons/sq km.

NOTE

• Census 2011: most populous state — Uttar Pradesh; least populous — Sikkim; highest literacy — Kerala; lowest — Bihar; highest sex ratio — Kerala; lowest — Haryana.

• Census is a Union subject, listed at entry 69 of the Union List, mentioned in Article 246.

question: Yamini Krishnamurthy is a famous exponent of which form of dance?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bharatnatyam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Yamini Krishnamurthy (1940–2024) was a celebrated exponent of Bharatanatyam, and also of Kuchipudi and Odissi. (भरतनाट्यम)

• She was honoured with the Padma Shri (1968), Padma Bhushan (2001) and Padma Vibhushan (2016), and was named Asthana Nartaki (resident dancer) of the Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams.

• Bharatanatyam is the classical dance of Tamil Nadu, based on the Natya Shastra of Bharata Muni, and was earlier known as Sadir/Dasiattam.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Odissi — classical dance of Odisha; exponents: Kelucharan Mohapatra, Sonal Mansingh, Sanjukta Panigrahi.

• Mohiniyattam — classical dance of Kerala; exponents: Sunanda Nair, Bharati Shivaji, Kalamandalam Kalyanikutty Amma.

• Bihu — a folk dance of Assam, not a classical form.

NOTE

• The 8 classical dances: Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (Uttar Pradesh), Kathakali & Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur), Sattriya (Assam).

• Other Bharatanatyam exponents: Rukmini Devi Arundale, Balasaraswati, Padma Subrahmanyam, Mallika Sarabhai.

question: Akbar’s revenue system “Zabt” was developed by ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Todar Mal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Zabt (Zabti) system, also called the Dahsala system or Todar Mal’s Bandobast (1580), was developed by Raja Todar Mal, Akbar’s finance minister (Diwan-i-Ashraf). (ज़ब्त प्रणाली)

• Under it, the average produce and average prices of the previous 10 years were calculated, and one-third of the average produce was fixed as the state’s share, payable in cash.

• Land was surveyed and classified into four categories — Polaj, Parauti, Chachar and Banjar — according to its continuity of cultivation.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Bairam Khan — Akbar’s regent (1556–1560) who won the Second Battle of Panipat (1556) against Hemu.

• Raja Bharmal of Amber — the first Rajput ruler to accept Mughal suzerainty; his daughter married Akbar.

• Raja Man Singh — Akbar’s general who led the Mughal army in the Battle of Haldighati (1576) against Maharana Pratap.

NOTE

• Todar Mal was one of Akbar’s Navaratnas (nine gems), which also included Abul Fazl, Faizi, Tansen, Birbal, Man Singh, Abdul Rahim Khan-i-Khanan, Mulla Do-Piyaza and Fakir Aziao-Din.

• Other Mughal revenue systems: Kankut, Batai (Ghalla-Bakhshi) and Nasaq.

question: The number of live births per thousand persons in a year is called ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Birth rate.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The birth rate (crude birth rate, CBR) is the number of live births per 1,000 persons of the population in a year. (जन्म दर)

• The death rate (crude death rate, CDR) is the number of deaths per 1,000 persons in a year; the difference between birth rate and death rate gives the natural growth rate of population.

• In India, birth and death rates are estimated by the Sample Registration System (SRS) of the Registrar General of India.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Total Fertility Rate (TFR) — the average number of children a woman would bear in her reproductive life; India’s TFR fell to 2.0 (NFHS-5), below the replacement level of 2.1.

• Infant Mortality Rate (IMR) — deaths of infants below one year per 1,000 live births.

• Maternal Mortality Ratio (MMR) — maternal deaths per 1,00,000 live births.

NOTE

• The rapid growth of India’s population after 1921 is because 1921 is called the ‘Demographic Divide’ or the Great Divide year, after which the death rate fell sharply while the birth rate stayed high.

• NFHS-5 (2019–21) reported a sex ratio of 1,020 women per 1,000 men in India.

question: In June 2022, the “Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs” has approved deregulation of ______.
option_3: Sale of Domestically Produced Crude Oil
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sale of Domestically Produced Crude Oil.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In June 2022, the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA), chaired by the Prime Minister, approved the deregulation of the sale of domestically produced crude oil, effective 1 October 2022. (घरेलू कच्चे तेल की बिक्री से नियंत्रण हटाना)

• Producers (including ONGC and Oil India) were freed from the earlier requirement to sell crude only to government-nominated refineries, and may now sell in the domestic market to any buyer; exports remain barred.

• The move was aimed at attracting investment in exploration and production (E&P) and at giving producers market-linked prices.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The CCEA is one of the key Cabinet Committees constituted by the Prime Minister; others include the Cabinet Committee on Security (CCS), on Political Affairs, on Investment and Growth, and on Parliamentary Affairs.

• India’s crude-oil policy is administered by the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas; the licensing regime is the Hydrocarbon Exploration and Licensing Policy (HELP) with the Open Acreage Licensing Policy (OALP).

• India is the third largest consumer/importer of crude oil in the world, after the USA and China.

NOTE

• Petrol was deregulated in June 2010 and diesel in October 2014; Mumbai High (offshore, Maharashtra) is India’s largest oil field, and Rajasthan’s Barmer (Mangala field) is a major onshore source.

question: Which among the following is the structural and fundamental unit of life?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Cell.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The cell is the structural and functional (fundamental) unit of life — the smallest unit capable of independent existence and of carrying out all life processes. (कोशिका)

• The cell was discovered by Robert Hooke in 1665 while examining a thin slice of cork; he described it in his book ‘Micrographia’.

• Anton van Leeuwenhoek first observed living cells (1674); the Cell Theory was proposed by M. J. Schleiden (1838) and Theodor Schwann (1839), and extended by Rudolf Virchow (1855) with *Omnis cellula-e cellula* — all cells arise from pre-existing cells.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Tissue — a group of similar cells performing a common function; it is one level above the cell.

• Enzymes — biological catalysts, mostly proteins, that speed up biochemical reactions.

• Hormones — chemical messengers secreted by endocrine glands and carried by blood.

NOTE

• Cell organelles: Mitochondria — powerhouse of the cell; Ribosome — protein factory; Lysosome — suicidal bag; Golgi body — packaging and dispatch; Chloroplast — kitchen of the cell.

• The largest cell is the ostrich egg; the longest cell is the nerve cell (neuron); the smallest human cell is the sperm.

question: ______ are the vessels which carry blood away from the heart to various organs of the body.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Arteries.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Arteries are thick-walled, elastic blood vessels that carry blood away from the heart to the various organs of the body. (धमनियाँ)

• Arteries carry oxygenated blood, with one exception — the pulmonary artery, which carries deoxygenated blood from the heart to the lungs.

• Arteries have no valves (blood flows under high pressure), whereas veins have valves to prevent the backflow of blood.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Veins carry blood towards the heart; they carry deoxygenated blood, except the pulmonary vein, which brings oxygenated blood from the lungs to the heart.

• Trachea (windpipe) is part of the respiratory system, not the circulatory system.

• Plasma is the liquid (fluid) part of blood, about 55% of blood volume, and is not a vessel.

NOTE

• The aorta is the largest artery in the human body; capillaries are the thinnest blood vessels where exchange of gases and nutrients takes place.

• The human heart has four chambers (2 atria, 2 ventricles); normal blood pressure is about 120/80 mm Hg; blood circulation was discovered by William Harvey.

question: The satellites orbit the earth in which of the following layers of the atmosphere?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Exosphere.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The exosphere is the outermost layer of the earth’s atmosphere, beyond about 400 km, from where the atmosphere merges with outer space; satellites orbit the earth in this layer. (बाह्यमंडल)

• It has extremely thin air with very light gases such as hydrogen and helium, so there is almost no drag on satellites.

• The layers of the atmosphere from the surface upward are: Troposphere → Stratosphere → Mesosphere → Thermosphere (Ionosphere) → Exosphere.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Troposphere — the lowest layer, where all weather phenomena (clouds, rain, storms) occur; average height about 13 km.

• Stratosphere — contains the ozone layer, which absorbs harmful ultraviolet rays; jet aircraft fly here because it is free of turbulence.

• Mesosphere — where meteors burn up; it has the lowest temperature of the atmosphere (about –10° to –90°C at the mesopause).

NOTE

• The Ionosphere/Thermosphere reflects radio waves back to the earth, enabling long-distance radio communication.

• Composition of air: Nitrogen ≈ 78%, Oxygen ≈ 21%, Argon ≈ 0.93%, Carbon dioxide ≈ 0.04%.

question: Who become Wisden’s Leading Cricketer in the world 2018?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Virat Kohli.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Virat Kohli was named Wisden’s Leading Cricketer in the World for 2018 — the third year in a row that he received the honour (2016, 2017 and 2018).

• The award is given annually by Wisden Cricketers’ Almanack, first published in 1864 by John Wisden, and often called the ‘Bible of Cricket’.

• In 2018 Kohli scored heavily in Tests and ODIs, including a memorable Test century at Perth during India’s tour of Australia.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Ben Stokes — Wisden’s Leading Cricketer in the World for 2019, after his heroics in the World Cup final and the Headingley Ashes Test.

• Kane Williamson — New Zealand’s captain who led his side in the 2019 World Cup final and won the inaugural World Test Championship (2021).

• Rohit Sharma — holds the record for the highest individual ODI score (264) and five ODI double centuries.

NOTE
